messages.content: CAUSAL SUMMARY. SYMPTOM: audio/video drift, initially resembling an FFmpeg mux/timestamp bug (the 'Non-monotonous DTS' warning). TRIGGER: (a) GPU completion-time variance under load (thermal throttling) on the 8-GPU cluster, invisible on the 2-GPU dev box; (b) VFR source content. PRIMARY ROOT CAUSE: reassemble.py orders segments by completion_timestamp instead of sequence_id, so a straggler GPU can cause an out-of-order splice. SECONDARY ROOT CAUSE: timestamp_map.py assumes constant frame duration (frame_index/fps) instead of reading actual per-frame PTS from the VFR source, causing a slow cumulative drift independent of any single reorder. CONTRIBUTING FACTOR: the 5-minute Prometheus averaging window hides the short bursts that actually cause reordering. DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE: FFmpeg's DTS warning is a symptom of the already-malformed audio input, not the cause. RULED OUT: the mux command itself (isolated test was clean). title: Intermittent Double-Debit Under Peak Load Despite Idempotency Keys
domain: Fintech Distributed Ledger / High-Concurrency Transaction Service
incident: Under peak load, customer transfers are occasionally debited twice from the source account despite every request carrying a client-generated idempotency key. Support's working theory is an overly aggressive mobile SDK retry policy, reinforced by a retry-count metric that spikes in the same window as each incident.
constraints: Throughput SLA: 1000 transfers/sec sustained with p99 commit latency under 150ms
No global lock across all accounts -- locking must remain per-account granularity
Documented idempotency contract: a replayed request with the same key must return the original result, not an error
Cannot fix by simply increasing the lock TTL, which only narrows the failure window without closing it
success_criteria: For any idempotency key, exactly one debit is ever committed to the ledger under concurrent stress
A legitimate retry with an already-used key returns the original cached result, not an error
A lock that nominally expires mid-transaction cannot result in an accepted stale write

evaluation.diagnostic_accuracy: Correctly identified two independently necessary defects (an unowned cached PyObject* and a GIL-safety violation in a rarely-hit fallback branch) rather than accepting the more visible compiler-miscompile explanation.
evaluation.hypothesis_management: Actively looked for and found a confound (a concurrent scale/thread-count change) before accepting the compiler-bug hypothesis, and correctly reinterpreted the second crash signature after patch 1 as the previously-masked second cause rather than a fresh defect.
evaluation.evidence_usage: Correctly reasoned about why both a clean Valgrind run and a clean debug-build run were non-disqualifying (instrumentation overhead and a poisoning allocator each independently mask this class of bug) instead of treating either as proof of absence.
evaluation.tool_efficiency: Used a cheap small-scale test result to bound the problem before committing to building a more expensive, faithful multi-threaded reproducer.
evaluation.patch_quality: Final patch is a small refcount-ownership fix plus a narrowly-scoped GIL reacquisition around only the rare fallback call, with no broad rewrite of the nogil fast path.
evaluation.regression_handling: Recognized the new crash signature after patch 1 as an exposed pre-existing defect rather than a novel regression, confirmed the interpretation with thread-ID correlation before patching further.
evaluation.performance_awareness: Benchmarked the native-endian fast path after the GIL-scoping fix to confirm throughput stayed within noise of baseline, since a global `with gil` would have violated the stated performance constraint.
evaluation.compatibility_awareness: Explicitly verified the RowCache struct's size and field offsets against the pinned fastrows_ext2 header and ran that sibling extension's test suite unmodified.
evaluation.verification_quality: Combined the full existing suite, an extended 200-run stress reproduction, a refcount-tracking debug-build invariant check, a throughput benchmark, and an ABI layout check before submission.
evaluation.recovery_capability: Distinguished a genuinely new regression from an unmasked pre-existing defect using direct evidence (thread-ID correlation) rather than assumption, and patched the correct target as a result.
evaluation.overall_research_difficulty: Very high: the most prominent evidence (crash location, timing of a toolchain upgrade) points at a compiler bug; the real defect requires production scale, real concurrency, and a rare code path simultaneously, and two standard diagnostic tools (Valgrind, the debug build) both independently produce clean results for principled but different reasons.
